h1: Pannapat Place — A Genuinely Spacious Budget Service Apartment on Soi Phahonyothin 35, Bangkok
intro: When most budget hotels in the Kaset neighbourhood pack guests into small rooms, Pannapat Place quietly delivers something different: service-apartment-sized rooms with private balconies at prices that parents visiting Kasetsart University students — or anyone with business in north Bangkok — can actually afford. Sitting at 181/11 Soi Phahonyothin 35, Lat Yao, Chatuchak, BTS Ratchayothin (Green Line) is around 600 m away, a comfortable eight-minute walk. The property has 75 rooms and has been running since 2011. From around ฿700 per night, and scoring 8.9/10 from 373 Trip.com reviews, it is a consistently well-regarded address in a neighbourhood that rewards those who look past the central-Bangkok postcode.

body.html: A long-standing address in the neighbourhood — Pannapat Place opened in 2011 on Soi Phahonyothin 35, a residential side-street in Lat Yao, Chatuchak, a short drive from the Bangkhen campus of Kasetsart University. With 75 rooms it is larger than the boutique guesthouses dotting the same soi, and its service-apartment format means you get noticeably more floor space per baht than a conventional hotel at the same price point. A score of 8.9/10 from 373 Trip.com reviews — accumulated over more than a decade — confirms that Pannapat Place has maintained its standard consistently, not just in the glow of a recent renovation.

Location and getting around — Soi Phahonyothin 35 runs inward from Phahonyothin Road. BTS Ratchayothin station (Green Line) is roughly 600 m away, an eight-minute walk — a touch further than some competitors in the area, but well within range without needing a motorbike taxi. From Ratchayothin, Siam is about 25 minutes by BTS; Mo Chit and Chatuchak Market are just a few stops. Major Ratchayothin (department store, cinema, restaurants) is walkable in around 15 minutes. A 7-Eleven sits directly beside the hotel — a detail that appears in more than a few reviews as a genuine convenience for late-night arrivals or early-morning departures. Kasetsart University Bangkhen is a five-minute drive or about 20–25 minutes on foot. Don Mueang Airport (DMK) is roughly 12–14 km, around 20–25 minutes by car.
"Big room for the price, soft bed, clean bathroom, friendly check-in staff — free parking was a genuine bonus for us driving from out of town."

Rooms and amenities — Four room types are on offer: Superior Double (non-smoking), Superior Twin (non-smoking), Triple Room, and Deluxe. Every room comes with air conditioning, a fridge, LCD TV, free Wi-Fi, a private bathroom with hot shower, and — the feature that recurs most in positive reviews — a private balcony. The latter is an uncommon amenity at this price level and guests consistently describe it as a welcome touch, particularly in the evening. General room condition is praised for cleanliness and larger-than-expected floor space. Points to note from real reviews: the bathroom can feel cramped compared with the rest of the room, and lighting in some rooms is dimmer than ideal for reading or desk work.

Services and on-site facilities — The front desk runs 24 hours; check-in is described as quick and pleasant. Free on-site parking is a recurring highlight for guests arriving by car — a meaningful differentiator in a city where hotel parking charges add up. Laundry service, luggage storage, and taxi booking are available. There is no restaurant on-site, but the 7-Eleven next door covers basics at any hour, and the surrounding streets offer street food and local restaurants at student-friendly prices. The in-building washing machine is noted in some reviews as a practical plus for longer stays. Wi-Fi is free throughout, though a handful of reviews flag inconsistent speeds — worth bearing in mind if you plan to work remotely.

What real guests say — Compiled from Trip.com (373 reviews, 8.9/10) and TripAdvisor (31 reviews, 3.9/5). Consistently praised: spacious, clean rooms that exceed expectations for the rate; soft beds and good sleep quality; warm and helpful reception staff; fast check-in; free parking; and the 7-Eleven immediately next door. Recurring caveats: narrow bathroom with a cramped shower area; Wi-Fi can be inconsistent — a mobile hotspot backup is recommended for heavy data users; some ground-floor rooms are susceptible to outside noise; and the soi location means the BTS walk, while manageable, is longer than at a couple of competing properties in the area.

Pricing and value — Superior Double and Twin rooms start from around ฿700–800 per night in regular periods, climbing toward ฿1,000–1,200 during public holidays or events tied to Kasetsart University (graduation season, fairs). For a service apartment offering a private balcony, free parking, and 75 rooms' worth of operational consistency, that represents clear value in this part of Bangkok. Pannapat Place is best suited to parents visiting the university, business travellers with meetings around Ratchayothin or Ngam Wong Wan, or anyone wanting a quiet, roomy base in north Bangkok without paying for a central-city address.

honestSummary: Pannapat Place earns its place as the best-value spacious-room option in the Kaset neighbourhood — wide rooms, private balconies, free parking, friendly staff, and a sub-฿1,000 rate. Honest downsides: narrow bathrooms, inconsistent Wi-Fi, and a BTS walk that is a minute or two longer than some nearby alternatives.
honestChecks: If you need reliable Wi-Fi for video calls or remote work — several reviews flag inconsistent speeds. Bring mobile data as a backup or ask the hotel about signal quality in your specific room before committing.
If you are sensitive to noise — some ground-floor rooms pick up sounds from the soi. Ask for an upper floor at check-in; this is usually granted if rooms are available.

If your primary goal is sightseeing around Siam, Sukhumvit, or Chinatown — Kaset is in north Bangkok; BTS travel to central areas takes 25–40 minutes. This property suits people with business or family reasons to be in the Kaset-Ratchayothin zone, not tourists on a city-centre itinerary.

tips.title: BTS Ratchayothin — 8 min walk or a quick motorbike taxi
tips.body: Exit the soi onto Phahonyothin Road and follow it to Ratchayothin BTS station (Green Line). From there you can reach Mo Chit and Chatuchak Park in two stops, or Siam in around 25 minutes.

tips.title: Share your GPS pin with Grab or taxi drivers
tips.body: Soi Phahonyothin 35 runs quite deep into the block and the hotel sign is not highly visible from Phahonyothin Road. Drop a pin in Grab or tell your driver 'Soi Phahon Yothin 35, near Major Ratchayothin' for the clearest directions.

tips.title: Request an upper floor if noise is a concern
tips.body: Ground-floor rooms can catch soi noise, particularly in the evening. A quick request at check-in for a higher floor usually works if rooms are available.

tips.title: No hotel restaurant — but 7-Eleven is right next door
tips.body: The 7-Eleven directly beside the building handles breakfast basics, late-night snacks, and drinks 24 hours. Local rice-and-noodle shops are scattered along the surrounding streets at very affordable prices.

faq.q: Where is Pannapat Place and how close is it to the BTS?
faq.a: Pannapat Place is at 181/11 Soi Phahon Yothin 35, Lat Yao, Chatuchak, Bangkok 10900. BTS Ratchayothin station (Green Line) is approximately 600 m away — about an 8-minute walk. A motorbike taxi from the soi entrance gets you there in two to three minutes.

faq.q: What does a room at Pannapat Place cost?
faq.a: Standard Superior Double and Twin rooms start from around ฿700–800 per night in off-peak periods. Prices can rise to ฿1,000–1,200 during public holidays or university events. Compare rates across Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com before booking — prices sometimes differ.

faq.q: Is there free parking at Pannapat Place?
faq.a: Yes — free on-site parking is available for guests. This is one of the most-mentioned positives in guest reviews and a key reason the property appeals to travellers arriving by private car from outside Bangkok.

faq.q: Who is Pannapat Place best suited to?
faq.a: It is ideal for parents visiting children at Kasetsart University, business travellers with meetings in the Ratchayothin–Ngam Wong Wan corridor, and anyone wanting spacious rooms with a private balcony at under ฿1,000 per night. It is less suited to tourists whose main priority is proximity to central Bangkok sightseeing.

faq.q: Is there a restaurant at Pannapat Place?
faq.a: There is no hotel restaurant, but a 7-Eleven is immediately next door (open 24 hours), and the surrounding streets have plenty of Thai rice and noodle shops at budget-friendly prices. Major Ratchayothin with multiple food-court and restaurant options is around 15 minutes on foot.
